sections.body_md:
Time-domain specs say how fast a step rises and how much it overshoots. Frequency-domain specs say the same things in the language of \(L(j\omega)\), \(S\), and \(T\). Bandwidth is where the closed-loop map \(T\) has dropped 3 dB. Gain crossover is where \(|L| = 1\). Phase margin is how far the phase of \(L\) sits from \(-180^\circ\) at that crossover. Peak sensitivity is how close the Nyquist curve comes to \(-1\).

These are design targets. A loop that is large at low frequency tracks and rejects disturbances. A loop that is small at high frequency refuses sensor noise. The crossover is the compromise, and the phase there decides how oscillatory the compromise is.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
For a first-order loop, \(\omega_b = 1/\tau\) and the 10% to 90% rise time is about \(2.2/\omega_b\).

When \(|L| = 1\), the distance from that point to \(-1\) is \(2\sin(\mathrm{PM}/2)\), so
\[
|S| = \frac{1}{2\sin(\mathrm{PM}/2)}
\]
at crossover. This is the sensitivity at one frequency. The peak \(M_s\) is at least this large. The clearance from the Nyquist curve to \(-1\) is \(1/M_s\).

If \(L\) is real and positive, \(|S| = 1/(1+L)\) and \(|T| = L/(1+L)\). A demand \(|S| \le 0.25\) then asks for \(L \ge 3\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A phase margin of \(48^\circ\) puts the crossover sensitivity at \(1/(2\sin 24^\circ)\). Since \(\sin 24^\circ \approx 0.407\), the sensitivity is about \(1.23\). That is already above 1, so the Nyquist curve is not far from \(-1\), but it is not a 30-degree design either. A first-order bandwidth of 10 rad/s would rise from 10% to 90% in about \(2.2/10 = 0.22\) s. The two numbers are a speed target and a damping target, and a later loop-shape has to meet both at once.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: Crossover of \(L\) is not the bandwidth of \(T\), though they are often near each other. The crossover formula gives \(|S|\) at one frequency, not automatically the peak over all frequencies. Phase margin is not the phase: a 50 degree margin means the phase is \(-130^\circ\), not \(-50^\circ\). And a larger allowed \(M_s\) is a weaker robustness spec, because it permits the curve to pass closer to \(-1\).

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Loop shaping moves \(\omega_c\), the slope near crossover, and the low-frequency gain until these targets are met. Fundamental limits then say how high \(\omega_c\) can go before a right-half-plane zero, a delay, or the Bode sensitivity integral makes the spec impossible.
